clue.text: Like an essay of note in The Scotsman

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the word for the Scotsman, splitting it open

parts.note: Mac is a familiar crossword name for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A remark about a note on some essay published in the Edinburgh newspaper The Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' reads as the Edinburgh newspaper's title, but it splits into two pieces, and 'in' places the note inside the word for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a composition on a single theme, so something like one is organised around a subject.

clue.text: Had a nice renovated country house in Spain

indicators.note: a renovated building has been reworked, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone owned a pleasant restored villa in rural Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges the letters of HAD A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is the Spanish word for a large estate with its main dwelling, used for a ranch house.

clue.text: Isle's English ministerial residence

parts.note: the Isle of Man, with its possessive, gives MAN'S

explanation.surface: A minister's house on a British island described as English.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; its possessive gives MAN'S, and the apostrophe drops out in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in Scottish Presbyterian churches.

clue.text: Extremes of Marsupialia, as seen in remarkable island native

definitions.text: Extremes of Marsupialia, as seen in remarkable island native

indicators.note: the picked letters are seen within the rearranged fodder, placed inside it
remarkable here means worthy of remark but signals the fodder being remade into a new order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of the zoological order's name

explanation.surface: A zoological note: the ends of the marsupial order show up in a striking animal found only on one island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges the last two words, and 'as seen in' places the marsupial's outer letters inside them. The whole clue also describes the animal, found wild only on Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: This carnivorous marsupial survives in the wild only on Tasmania, so it is both a marsupial and a striking native of an island.

clue.text: Most comfortable Greek island site developed

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: a developed site has been built up and changed, so the word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Holiday advice: the snuggest spot is a newly built resort on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the last word, and the result follows the island. Cos is also spelt Kos.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy means snug and comfortable, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Point that's put right on the map

definitions.meaning: one of the four cardinal points of the compass
maps are normally drawn with north at the top, so this direction lies to the right

explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal direction is a compass point, and on a north-up map it is shown on the right-hand side.

clue.text: It's enough to take one's breath away

definitions.text: It's enough to take one's breath away

parts.words: It's enough to take one's breath away
parts.note: the idiom for being astonished is read literally, as a lung disease that leaves the sufferer breathless

explanation.definitionFit: This disease damages the air sacs of the lungs and causes chronic breathlessness.

clue.text: Queen grabbed by rook in file

indicators.note: the queen's letter is held inside the word for the swindle

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle them, and a sting is a swindle
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A chess scene: the queen is taken by a rook on one of the board's files.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words mislead: 'rook' is to swindle, giving STING, and 'grabbed by' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a line of things one behind another, as is a string of items.

clue.text: It displays a collection of side tables

definitions.text: It displays a collection of side tables

parts.words: It displays a collection of side tables
parts.note: side here means a sports team and tables are league standings, not pieces of furniture

explanation.definitionFit: England's professional soccer competition publishes standings for its member clubs.

clue.text: Emotional outbursts in parts of play

definitions.meaning: making a scene means a public display of temper
a play is divided into acts and these smaller sections

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both public displays of strong feeling and the subdivisions of a drama.

clue.text: Sunday headgear seen in Cork?

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone's Sunday-best hat is spotted in the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city, but the question mark points to a bottle cork, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork is one kind of bung used to seal a bottle, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: One thrown out by brethren, e.g. a deserter

indicators.note: the answer stands by, or among, the letters of the following words, which hold it inside them

explanation.surface: An excommunicated member of a religious brotherhood, for instance one who deserted it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'brethREN, E.G. A DEserter'; the religious surface makes 'deserter' look like the definition, but its first letters are part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade has broken with a group and is treated as an outcast by it.

clue.text: Hearing's difficult

definitions.meaning: a court ... a case is hearing it
as in a ... day, one that tests patience

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the court's act of judging a case and an adjective for something wearing or hard to bear.

clue.text: Run commercial property said to store cars

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the cars inside them, as a depot stores vehicles

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: the word for the characteristic is given as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: a property in the sense of a characteristic is a trait
Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: Operate a business site that is meant to keep vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives the sound of the word for a characteristic, not its spelling; 'to store' puts the cars inside the advert plus that sound. The Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an organisation is to manage or direct its affairs.

clue.text: Strange item newspapers etc, will break next

indicators.note: the media word breaks into the rearranged letters, splitting them
something strange is out of its usual order, so the letters of item are rearranged

parts.note: the press and broadcasting together are the media

explanation.surface: An odd news item about the press is about to break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the first word, and 'will break' splits that arrangement after its second letter to admit the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate can mean nearest in order, as in the immediate successor, the very next one.

clue.text: Nearly everyone getting ready to fight? That's scary!

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: all means everyone
arming is taking up weapons in readiness for battle

explanation.surface: A nation where almost everybody is taking up weapons is a frightening thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of the word for everyone; 'That's' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening is disturbing and causes alarm.

clue.text: Curt utterance — could be yes or no, not maybe

definitions.text: Curt utterance — could be yes or no, not maybe

parts.words: Curt utterance — could be yes or no, not maybe
parts.note: a short reply of a single sound unit, as two of these replies have one syllable while the third has two

explanation.definitionFit: A word of one syllable is the shortest sort of utterance, like a terse reply.

clue.text: Mix drink and bring in fish

indicators.note: the drinking word brings the fish inside itself

parts.note: to sup is to drink
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Instructions to blend a cocktail and then fetch some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' with 'drink' suggests a milkshake, but the drink is the verb to sup, and 'bring in' puts the fish inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a mixing or reorganisation, as when a company's departments are rearranged.

clue.text: Disc produced by group

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a round flat shape and a set of people with a shared interest.

clue.text: Trifle made by cook

definitions.meaning: to trifle is to ... about idly with something
to cook the books is to falsify accounts

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to play idly with something and to falsify figures dishonestly.

clue.text: Fissure formed by a lively Yorkshire river

parts.note: pert means sprightly or lively
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A gap in the rock carved by a fast-flowing river in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure runs through North Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an opening or gap, a crack being a narrow kind of hole.

clue.text: One in special pack to chase vermin up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rat is a classic example of vermin

explanation.surface: A dog in a pack of hunters runs off to chase rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TO followed by RAT, giving the letters bottom to top in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single card of the fortune-teller's deck is called by the same name as the deck itself.

clue.text: China, girl's cup

parts.note: CH is the international abbreviation for China
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's cup made of porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' seems to be porcelain, but here it is the country's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially one used for communion wine.

clue.text: Herb adding taste, we hear, to fish

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: the tasting word is given as it sounds, then spelt differently

parts.note: to lick something is to taste it

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: flavour the fish with a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: GAR then LIC, the sound of 'lick'. Garlic is strictly a bulb, but cooks class it with herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a pungent plant of the onion family used as a flavouring, loosely grouped with herbs.

clue.text: Name genealogist starts with

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following word supply the answer

explanation.surface: Asking for the forename that a family-history researcher begins with.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four letters of 'genealogist' make a man's name; the surface suggests asking a researcher for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene is a man's forename, short for Eugene.

clue.text: Unorthodox priest, say, with backing and reputation

indicators.note: an unorthodox cleric strays from the norm, so the word's letters stray into a new order
the abbreviation for 'for example' is turned around

parts.note: e.g., for example, is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: A nonconforming cleric, for instance, who has support and a good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodox' rearranges the cleric, and 'backing' turns round the abbreviation for 'for example', which 'say' stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is the standing or high regard someone earns, much like good name.
